- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.75), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–3% of recent mean.
- Model consistently under-responds to sharp upward sentiment spikes; if last 3 sentiment values include ≥ 2 spikes above 0.75, add 2–5% to forecast for next 3 periods.
- Model over-anticipates downward moves after negative sentiment; if last sentiment includes ≥ 2 values ≤ -0.50, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3 periods.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if recent 5-day forecast is 2% above true, adjust next forecast down by 1–2% unless sentiment is strong positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 2–4 days; if true outcome shows upward momentum, forecast should be adjusted up by 1–3% for next 3 days.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model forecast exceeds true outcome by > 2% for 2 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low volatility (e.g., 0.8, -0.6, 0.9), model tends to overfit short-term noise; apply smoothing filter to reduce 3-day forecast variance.
